# NOTES: 3 BOOKS

## BOOK 1: The Boy Traders; or, The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers (Harry Castlemon; Frank Nelson Series; Stranger schooner)

**Characters**
- Uncle Dick (captain of schooner *Stranger*; old sailor, gray hair, meerschaum pipe, jolly, stern when needed)
- Frank Nelson (sailing master; ex-whaler Tycoon commander after Capt. Barclay wounded)
- Archie Winters (Frank's cousin; boastful, brave; Maynard rifle; wild horse lasso; "Rocky Mountains 100 miles from NY" joke)
- Walter Gaylord (paymaster, keeps safe key; plantation heir)
- Eugene Gaylord (Walter's brother; flute; Henry rifle; Bellville)
- Fred Craven; George Le Dell; "Featherweight" (nickname); Perk (Phil Perkins; cook at times)
- Dick Lewis (trapper, backwoodsman, Indian yells, fast runner, "Human natur'!"); Bob Kelly (trapper)
- Mr. Baldwin (first mate); Mr. Parker (second mate); Lucas (old boatswain's mate); Barton (coxswain); Rodgers; Brown (sailor); "Doctor" (negro cook); Freas
- Chase and Wilson (absent Club members in Bellville; later orange plantation in Florida)
- Waters (giant escaped English convict, "hif"); Bob (ticket-of-leave convict, gold-bought freedom); other convicts
- Fowler (consul's clerk, "Aw!", drawl, gold eyeglass)
- Mr. Wilbur (sheep-station owner, Uncle Dick's friend; Tasmania/Australia)
- Mack/McGregor (Scottish transport-rider, Natal guide; stole Walter's horse and gun, sold Uncle Dick's horse/gun, fled)
- Mynheer Schrader (surly Boer field cornet)
- Jones (Kaffir-named gun owner; Frank fixes gun)
- Griqua and Zulu chiefs; Kaffir servants (deserted)
- Lieutenant (gray-headed), Midshipman Kendall (Royal Navy)
- Sea Gull (wrecked English ship); the "Strangers" (rescued men)
- Pike, Zack, Silas (earlier trappers, Archie's old story)

**Events (in order)**
1. Sandwich Islands: barometer, cyclone quiz with Frank. Honolulu; Frank's Tycoon story. Club rides around Oahu. Hilo: surf-board dare; Archie/Eugene back down. Kilauea volcano: trappers stay on veranda; boys descend crater. Trappers decide to go to Africa with Uncle Dick.
2. Gale: Frank sails to Mangroves; Long Tom (30-pdr) fires at natives (shell); anchor. Gale: Dick Lewis's "quid" fear; "Davy Jones's locker"; Frank navigates away from lee shore; cabin battened; schooner damaged (jibboom, topmasts gone).
3. Four weeks peaceful; cyclone warning; Mr. Baldwin explains storm; Stranger escapes. Second storm 3 days; dismantled; drifts to island; Long Tom thrown overboard; ship Sea Gull wreck; natives in canoes; shrapnel from 24-pdr sinks canoe; boys pump; passage through breakers; anchor.
4. Sea Gull survivors (11 rescued by boats; Archie counts); Waters identified among them. Frank watch; "Dick Lewis" can subdue; Hobart Town destination (Van Diemen's Land).
5. Waters swaggers; Parker orders him forward; Waters strikes Lucas; attacks; Dick Lewis throws him; master-at-arms irons him; sent to brig; Uncle Dick lectures the 3 suspected men. Race idea. Decision: Natal, not Japan.
6. Hobart Town: Waters sees city, identifies; convicts confined. Fowler arrives ("consul's clerk"); Frank refuses Fowler's demand; police boat takes convicts. Bendigo mines anecdote (ounce of gold bribe to police). Fowler dinner; Archie's "mountains" joke.
7. Mr. Wilbur's sheep farm: Dick vs Eugene's horse race (Dick wins, gives horse flying start). Melbourne trip; Archie's horse stolen by bushrangers. Hobart return; Fowler questions Frank about paymaster, safe, navigation. Schooner in river; Frank locked in cabin; ship taken by convicts (Waters, Bob, Fowler; Brown, two others mutinous). Frank's watch; convicts' history.
8. Plot revealed: Fowler lured Walter; Bob to kidnap; Archie captured as Walter (Panama hat). Frank forced to command. Doctor kept aboard. Sailors discharged later.
9. Frank's Yankee trick: passes steamer (man-of-war) with lights out. Archie hands Frank revolver; irons Waters while asleep; takes Bob's revolvers; recaptures ship with Brown, Stevens, Doctor, negro cook. Fowler irons. Waters offers Doctor £1000 bribe.
10. Man-of-war arrives (English flag run up; Frank refuses to haul US flag). Lieutenant boards; Kendall. Convicts transferred; schooner sails to Hobart under US flag; tug with Club, Uncle Dick, Wilbur arrives. Three foremast hands discharged (Brown and others).
11. Voyage to Natal; Wilbur family cruise; Africa sighted.
12. Grahamstown: Mack (McGregor) hired; colonel's outfit (elephant gun, wagon 18 ft, oxen, horses, camp stools). Lottery for guns and horses: Frank draws No. 3 (vicious horse, heavy rifle); Archie gets silver-mounted rifle, thoroughbred. Kaffir servants (cook, thief).
13. Trek; Boers; Mynheer Schrader refuses trade; field cornet; Griqua visitors; Frank repairs gun for "Jones." Boers warn of lion veldt. Eugene dares Archie/Fred to shooting-hole overnight.
14. Shooting-hole at fountain: Archie, Fred, Eugene fire ~39 shots at "lions"; a pack of wild dogs (jackals as scouts). Uncle Dick and Frank come with torches; creature is a wild dog.
15. Lion-hunt aftermath; Boers refuse trade; Mack's suspicious manner; Archie's horse lost in thorn bush, found (Uncle Dick's horse calls it). Schrader warns Bushmen. Kaffirs threaten to desert.
16. Night: Kaffirs flee with guns and oxen; Mack steals Walter's horse and rifle, leaves ("deserted"). Perk makes breakfast; Walter drives oxen. Trade with Griquas; ivory; chief's messenger returns. Zulu emissaries (~150 warriors) demand Uncle Dick's double-barrel; Dick Lewis's Indian yells and dance frighten them off.
17. Conclusion: Dick "medicine-man." Griquas return with corn. Zulu ambush at dry stream: Bob's rifle kills chief; Archie's horse killed, Frank saves Archie; spear hits Frank's haversack (cartridges). Trade with Boers at return; eighty oxen; Mack sold horse and gun in Grahamstown and fled. Homeward; Bellville; Gaylord mansion; festivities.
18. Epilogue: Frank a lawyer in Lawrence; Archie civil engineer, married; Chase & Wilson orange plantation Florida; Fred revenue service lieutenant; Jasper Babcock commission merchant Bellville; George Le Dell in Memphis; Phil Perkins steamers New Orleans–Galveston; Walter & Eugene run Gaylord plantation; Uncle Dick cabin; Banner and Stranger still afloat.

## BOOK 2: The Red Rat's Daughter (Guy Boothby, 1899, illus. Henry Austin)

**Characters**
- John Grantham Browne (28, bachelor; wealth £120,000/yr; "Browne's Mimosa Soap" joke; cynical wit; father old Brown, soap-boiler, died; mother Rushbrooke daughter)
- Katherine Petrovitch (real name Polowski; painter; Russian; income £300/yr; shares with Madame; mother Hungarian, died when K was 7; father Stefan, Nihilist, sent to Siberia, then Saghalien)
- Madame Sophie Bernstein (stout, ruby velvet, diamonds, false; Katherine's guardian; secretly, husband = "Red Rat" Kleinkopf, diamond-thief)
- Felix Maas (cosmopolitan, pale, cough; actually a traitor/spy; sabotages engine; sends "Maas"; drugged; landed at Tomari)
- Jimmy Foote (small, shrewd, loyal; "my dear old Jack")
- Duchess of Matlock; Lady Iseult, Lady Imogen; Miss Verney; Hon. Silas Dobson (US Ambassador); Mrs. Dobson; George Barrington-Marsh
- Herr Otto Sauber (old seedy German, Hong-kong contact)
- Johann Schmidt (Hong-kong curio dealer; German; pipe)
- MacAndrew (tall Oxford-educated adventurer; Hong-kong; rescues Stefan; fee £5000 gold)
- Captain Mason (yacht skipper, red face, beard); M'Cartney (chief engineer); Phillips (third mate); second engineer (confessed)
- Bretherton (lawyer, Chancery Lane); Alphonse (Lallemand's); Bramthwaite (Gibraltar officer)
- Herr Stefan Polowski/"Petrovitch" (escaped convict, small red-haired man, ill)

**Events (in order)**
1. Merok (Gieranger Fjord, Norway); yacht *Lotus Blossom* (1200 tons). Waterfall walk; fog; Browne finds Katherine on hillside above precipice; coat-lowering rescue; carries her to road; Madame arrives; "Browne's Mimosa Soap" line.
2. Dinner; Foote's yarns; Browne/Maas talk on marriage; Russia notion (Demetrovitch). Browne visits hotel, Madame; Maas in hotel. Yacht leaves Merok.
3. Six months later (March), London: fog; Browne buys water-colour of Merok at Waterloo Place; address 43 German Park Road. Studio visit; tea; Katherine says she won't meet in Petersburg; Covent Garden *Lohengrin* dinner (Lallemand's, No. 6 box).
4. Browne tells Foote he loves her; Jimmy joins dinner; Madame "stares." Browne calls Warwick Road; Katherine and Madame left for Paris at nine. Maid gives address (35 Rue Jacquarie, Paris). Browne follows by 11 am train.
5. Paris: Rue Jacquarie; Amphitryon Club; Maas. Rue des Tuileries meeting; Katherine: "let me know when leaving Paris." Madame's pink-paper note (Thursday). Madame: "Katherine loves you," wants him to leave. Katherine enters; Browne proposes; she confesses love; Madame "approves." Fontainebleau day planned; Maison Dorée dinner.
6. Browne buys plain gold ring; Fontainebleau trip (rain then sun; ring on her finger on train). Next morning letter: she refuses marriage. Browne goes to Rue Jacquarie; Madame distressed. Louvre Room IV (Titian *Entombment*); Katherine's tale: father Polowski, mother Petrovitch's sister's name; father's escape plan; uncle's inheritance £300/yr. Browne vows to help on condition of marriage.
7. Browne consults Sauber (Madame's old friend, warns of Madame's indiscretion); Sauber gives address of Johann Schmidt in Hong-kong. Katherine demands Browne not tell Madame plans; Browne promises. Browne leaves Paris; meets Maas on Calais boat.
8. Browne makes will leaving estate to Katherine (Bretherton). Browne tells Foote; Foote joins ("I'm coming with you"). Yacht sails from Southampton (Captain Mason). Maas invites himself (feigned ill lungs); Maas reveals he knew from acquaintance of Polowski's name.
9. Paris reunion; Katherine and Madame to Marseilles; Browne sees them off on mail-boat. Yacht Lotus sails; Swanage; Gibraltar (Browne lunches with Bramthwaite); Port Said; Aden; Colombo; Singapore; Hong-kong (Club; Schmidt's shop; MacAndrew's visit with plan; £5000 gold in two boxes). Envelope with plan vanishes from cabin (Maas suspected).
10. Yokohama: Katherine; Madame; two-week wait; Maas aboard. Maas admits he knew plan ("Polowski" = Red Rat's daughter); offers help; Foote distrusts.
11. Saghalien; Cape Siretoko; Bay of Kroptskoi hut; Browne waits; MacAndrew arrives with "Petrovitch" (red-haired, small, ill). Rocket signal; yacht picks them up; Mason's advice to wait till morning (fog, current).
12. Russian man-of-war appears; engine crosshead-pin removed (Maas bribed engineer); Frank's family analog: Maas caught; MacAndrew forces Maas to drink sedative. Stefan hidden in tail-shaft tunnel. Russian boat boards; inspection; Foote reports Maas's sedation; Russian officer says Kleinkopf is "Red Rat," diamond-thief. Madame faints.
13. Katherine asks Browne to release her; he refuses. MacAndrew reveals Red Rat = Madame's husband, died early last year (the "father" was not Katherine's father). Maas landed at Tomari (Kunashiri) in three months. MacAndrew leaves at Hakodate with Browne's envelope of money for Madame/Katherine.
14. Final: Browne and Katherine at night; "you are not THE RED RAT'S DAUGHTER!" END.

## BOOK 3: The O'Ruddy: A Romance (Stephen Crane & Robert Barr, 1903)

**Characters**
- Tom O'Ruddy ("The O'Ruddy"; narrator; 18 at start; Glandore, near Old Head of Kinsale; sword gift of King Louis; hot temper, lies, boasts)
- Father O'Ruddy (dead; old soldier, lied; "Mickey Clancy" steward; Father Donovan, priest; Father Corrigan)
- Earl of Westport (old, sick, bright eyes, cackles; papers; "Straw!")
- Lord Strepp (young heir, ~20, fair; honourable)
- Colonel Clarence Royale (~40, "uncle" of Lady Mary, gouty, duelling)
- Reginald Forister (dark-skinned Bristol man, Earl's shipping partner; "Nell"; duelist)
- Lady Mary Strepp (Earl's daughter; beloved; "God spare you!")
- Countess of Westport ("Hoity-Toity"; drunken, violent, shrill; wields ebony stick)
- Tompkins (Earl's valet); parrot ("Pretty lady!")
- Paddy (red-headed Irishman, hired/stand-in; huge hair; Irish; stick; clumsy, loyal, ogling)
- Jem Bottles (highwayman; mother; seven ballads; "Stand and deliver")
- Dame Bottles (his mother)
- Sir Edmund Flixton (duelist, fled)
- Fullbil (literary wit, old, growls); Bobbs (dramatist); Fancher (critic); Doctor Chord (small scientist, scandal-monger; Countess's "rum" cure; betrays; later "traitor")
- Josiah Brooks (lawyer, Temple; calm, dry; "Possession is nine points"); melancholy clerk
- Strammers (gardener; blunderbuss; "French pears"; Paddy/Jem bribe)
- Tom Peel (Rye smuggler, giant); Father Kilnane; Mike Sullivan (boxing champion); Sir Goddard Oxenbridge (dead witch at Brede; sawn in half; tunnel)
- Narrator's children (Patrick, Little Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan)

**Events (in order)**
1. Bristol: Glandore boyhood; father's death; papers; O'Ruddy travels to Bristol with papers for Earl. Inn "Pig and Turnip" (later London). Supper: Lord Strepp & Royale tell story of Earl's breeches lent to Earl in France; O'Ruddy shouts "That is a lie," challenges Royale. Lord Strepp visits; duel set. Night: Forister's insults; O'Ruddy boots Forister out of inn. Earl's arrival; Earl and Lady Mary (bright eyes) in hood; Earl: "Come to my chamber in the morning."
2. Night: O'Ruddy meets Paddy (keening); makes him stand-in; duel at dawn; Royale wounded (4 places); O'Ruddy laughs and spares him; Royale beaten by sobs; "lashings" confusion.
3. Papers stolen (Paddy had them); O'Ruddy chases Forister; highwayman Jem Bottles attacks; O'Ruddy takes Jem as guide; Dame Bottles; ride to Bath; Forister gone to Bristol; Forister in inn barricade (Paddy caught him); sword held; Paddy's chair scene; Bristol inn: Lord Strepp & Royale apologize; Earl's valet; Earl sneers "Straw!"; Lady Mary; Earl dismisses; papers seen in Earl's bed; O'Ruddy gives papers to Lady Mary.
4. Earl threatens O'Ruddy; Countess; parrot; garden summer-house; Lady Mary says don't fight Forister; O'Ruddy duels Forister (Forister shot-wounded left shoulder); "God spare you!" notes; Colonel's "uncle" talk; Forister's Nell; O'Ruddy sets trap; carriage robbed by Paddy & Jem; papers and gold recovered; Doctor Chord; Earl's Bath parlor; O'Ruddy tells Earl Lady Mary is his object.
5. Earl's Bath chamber; papers; Forister; Bath mob; O'Ruddy holds Lady Mary; Countess chases Paddy in Bristol/Bath; Lord Strepp & Royale at Bath; O'Ruddy at London "Pig and Turnip"; Fullbil's wit salon; Bobbs/Fancher; London drunk clergy (footmen parody); Jem sings ballad at Red Slipper.
6. Kensington Gardens: Doctor Chord's gossip; Lady Mary glance; Earl's town house (oak avenue); garden plan; climbing oak; Strammers' blunderbuss; Lady Mary's garden confession; Paddy & Jem beaten Sunday; O'Ruddy locked in Lady Mary's room; Countess; papers returned; Lady Mary's advice (Brooks in Temple); kiss; O'Ruddy meets Father Donovan in St Patrick's chapel (Patsy O'Gorman bequest £300; pilgrimage to Rome).
7. Doctor Chord treated Paddy/Jem with liniment; Chord flees; Brooks in Temple; £500 gold guineas (Lady Mary); Brooks' warnings; bogus papers; nine ruffians attack at night; O'Ruddy disarms all nine (sword-work), makes captain carry swords to "Pig and Turnip"; swords sent to Temple.
8. Father Donovan's Rye journey; Paddy's ambush on road; Jem's saddle roadside (Doctor Chord among ambushers). Rye: Tom Peel recruited (nine men, blunderbusses); Father Donovan rides with them; Brede House (caretaker; Sir Goddard legend); tunnel; Earl's attack; Lord Strepp leads; tunnel trap; Lord Strepp captured, released; Lord Strepp talks peace.
9. Paddy falls into trap-door; Manor House meeting: Earl, Countess, Lady Mary, Lord Strepp; Countess shakes Lady Mary; Lady Mary refuses ("I shall marry no man whom I do not love"); Countess relents; Lady Mary asks Father Donovan's blessing.
10. Wedding by Father Donovan; narrator writes memoirs with children. END.
